issue.title: xprompts.md Invoke section documents [[ ... ]] text blocks without the closing rule or the structural shorthand binding
issue.description:
The Invoke section of `sase/memory/xprompts.md` documents `[[ ... ]]` multi-line
text as an argument form but never states when the block closes, so an agent
reading only the memory note cannot tell whether a `]]` inside prose ends the
argument. Epic sase-sn made that rule canonical and shared across every Python
and Rust argument scanner, and it also changed how shorthand free text is bound,
which the note does not mention either.

Recorded as a PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP on sase-sn.6. The epic plan's "Out of scope"
section deliberately did not touch it, because memory files must not be edited
without explicit user permission in the conversation that requests it.

Closing this requires the project owner's explicit permission plus a
`sase memory init` run to regenerate `AGENTS.md` and the provider instruction
shims.

task_type_fields.proposed_change:
## Proposed change

In the Invoke bullet list, replace the bare
"`[[ ... ]]` multi-line text" mention with a wording that states the closing
rule and the shorthand binding, for example:

- Args: `#name(a, b)`, `#name(k=v)` (positional first), quoted comma/special
  values, `[[ ... ]]` multi-line text. A `[[` block closes at the first `]]`
  whose next non-whitespace character is an argument terminator (`,`, `)`, `}`,
  `|`, or end of the argument region); a `]]` anywhere else is content. A `]]`
  that must be followed by a terminator needs an explicit quoted argument
  instead.
- Shorthand free text (`#name: text`, `#name:: text`, `#name(args): text`) is
  bound structurally, not rewritten into `#name([[...]])` and re-lexed, so
  commas, `]]`, `+`, and unbalanced parens in prose stay inside the value.
  `+` decodes to a space only on the bare unquoted `#name:a,b` colon form.

Exact wording is the owner's call; `docs/xprompt.md` (Text Blocks section,
updated by this epic) is the authoritative long form to mirror.

payload.description: Epic sase-sn defined the closing rule and updated docs/xprompt.md; this note is the memory-file counterpart it could not edit
